div.head: I Cn 16.1
div.ab: ⁊ na þearf man na fæstan fram Eastran oð Pentecosten, butan hwa gescrifen sig oððe he elles fæstan wylle; eallswa of middanwintra oð octabas Epiphanige (þæt is seofon niht ofer Twelftan mæssdæge).
And ne þearf man fæsten fram Eastran oð Pentecosten, buton hwa gescryfen sy oððe he elles wille fæsten, and of middanwintra oð octabas Epiphanie.
⁊ na ðearf man na fæsten fram Eastron oð Pentecosten, buton hwa gescrifen sy oððe he elles fæsten wylle, ⁊ of middanwintre oð octabas Epiphanie.
Non sunt secundum legem indicta ieiunia a Pascha usque ad Pentecosten nec á natali Domini usque ad octauas Epiphanię, nisi qui per penitentiam uel sponte ieiunet.
⁊ na ðearf man na fæsten fram Eastron oð Pentecosten, buton hwa gescrifen sy oððe he elles fæsten wylle, ⁊ of middanwintre oð octabas Epiphanie.
And no man need fast from Easter till Pentecost— unless it has been prescribed to him as a penance or he desires to fast for some other reason—or from Christmas to the Octave of Epiphany.

Und man braucht nicht zu fasten von Ostern bis Pfingsten — ausser wenn einer mit Kirchenbusse belegt ist oder er sonst [freiwillig] fasten will — und (ebenso G) von Weihnachten bis Octave Epiphaniae (d. h. sieben Tage nach dem Zwölften [nach 6. Januar] Festtag G).

And there is no need to fast from Easter until Pentecost — unless someone has been given penance or otherwise [voluntarily] wishes to fast — and (likewise, G) from midwinter until the octave of Epiphany (that is, seven days after Twelfth Day [6 January], G).
div.note: G's ‘(þæt is seofon niht ofer Twelftan mæssedæge)’ is only in G and not original. Liebermann compares VI Atr 22.3.; Robertson (p. 139) takes I Cn from B, which begins at ‘mæssedæg’ in 14.2, the earlier clauses being supplied from G
